    NavElement

    NavElement is a VisualElement that registers a View address and owns its visibility lifecycle. Navigation Graph Show/Hide commands resolve this address through the runtime UIViewRegistry.

    <nav:NavElement name="main"
                view-category="Menu" view-key="Main"
                hide-on-back="false" block-back="false"
                follow-parent="true">
    <startup>
        <nav:UIViewStartupSettings on-start="InstantShow"
            hide-mode="Display"
            use-custom-start-position="false"
            auto-hide-after-show="false"
            auto-hide-delay="3" />
    </startup>
</nav:NavElement>

    Attributes

    Attribute Default Description
    view-category Default View catalog category
    view-key Empty Key within the selected category
    hide-on-back false Hides this visible View when it wins Back handling
    block-back false Consumes Back without hiding this View
    follow-parent true Follows the visibility of an enclosing NavElement

    Category and Key must both contain text. Comparison is ordinal and case-sensitive. The View registers only while attached to a Player-context panel and unregisters when detached.

    Startup settings

    On Start Initial behavior
    Disabled Uses the current resolved display state
    Instant Hide Starts hidden without animation
    Instant Show Starts visible without animation
    Animation Hide Starts visible and plays Hide
    Animation Show Starts hidden and plays Show

    The nested UIViewStartupSettings object accepts these attributes:

    Attribute Default Description
    on-start Disabled Initial behavior from the table above
    hide-mode Display Whether a hidden View leaves layout
    use-custom-start-position true Applies a pixel start translation before Move is prepared
    custom-start-position (0, 0, 0) Translation used when the custom start position is enabled
    auto-hide-after-show false Schedules Hide after Show finishes
    auto-hide-delay 3 Unscaled seconds before Auto Hide

    When Hidden selects Display (display: none, removed from layout) or Visibility (visibility: hidden, layout preserved). A Custom Start Position applies a pixel translate before Move values are prepared. Auto Hide after Show starts an unscaled timer only after Show finishes.

    See Transition animation for Show/Hide presets and manual channels.

    Nested Views and Back

    A nested NavElement with follow-parent="true" shows and hides with its nearest parent View. The parent waits for following children to settle before reporting completion. Set it to false when the child represents an independent overlay.

    hide-on-back and block-back participate before graph history. Enable only the behavior you intend; a visible View that consumes Back can prevent the active UI node's Use Back route.

    Runtime API

    NavElement view = root.Q<NavElement>("main");

view.Show();        // configured Show transition
view.Hide();        // configured Hide transition
view.InstantShow();
view.InstantHide();

Debug.Log($"{view.Id}: {view.IsVisible}");

    Visibility exposes the underlying UIViewVisibility for state events, scheduler selection, and direct Show/Hide UIAnimation settings. RestoreStartState() reapplies the configured startup state, and InvalidateAnimationStartValues() recaptures Move references after layout changes.

    If multiple NavElement instances register the same UIKey, a graph command intentionally fans out to all of them. Use distinct View keys when the instances must move independently.
